title: Encore Theater
paragraphs: A 1946 dramatic anthology based on true stories from medicine, including doctors, patients, research breakthroughs, and the personal costs of medical work.
Thirteen-program CBS summer dramatic anthology built around medicine, medical history, doctors, researchers and patients. Frozen GRH set contains the complete numbered run.
GRH documents the program through CBS/Schenley summer run (June 4, 1946 to August 27, 1946) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Frank Graham (announcer on 13 recordings), Jean Holloway (radio adaptor on 11 recordings and writer on 1 recording), Bill Lawrence (director on 11 recordings and producer on 11 recordings), Leith Stevens (conductor on 5 recordings, music on 3 recordings, composer on 1 recording, music score on 1 recording, and performer on 1 recording), [[person|lurene-tuttle|Lurene Tuttle]] (performer on 5 recordings), Norman Field (performer on 5 recordings), and Earle Ross (performer on 4 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include illness, patients and recovery, Schenley Laboratories sponsorship, medicine and medical practice, medical ethics, duty and sacrifice, medical-themed literary and film adaptation, and medical biography and history.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Postwar American medical and scientific interest, CBS 1946 summer replacement season, Schenley Laboratories sponsorship, and Complete surviving thirteen-program run.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]] (41 shared credited people), [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]] (21 shared credited people), [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]] (20 shared credited people), [[show|the-railroad-hour|The Railroad Hour]] (17 shared credited people), and [[show|the-halls-of-ivy|The Halls of Ivy]] (15 shared credited people).

A 1946 dramatic anthology based on true stories from medicine, including doctors, patients, research breakthroughs, and the personal costs of medical work.

Thirteen-program CBS summer dramatic anthology built around medicine, medical history, doctors, researchers and patients. Frozen GRH set contains the complete numbered run.

GRH documents the program through CBS/Schenley summer run (June 4, 1946 to August 27, 1946) on CBS Radio Network.

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Frank Graham (announcer on 13 recordings), Jean Holloway (radio adaptor on 11 recordings and writer on 1 recording), Bill Lawrence (director on 11 recordings and producer on 11 recordings), Leith Stevens (conductor on 5 recordings, music on 3 recordings, composer on 1 recording, music score on 1 recording, and performer on 1 recording), Lurene Tuttle (performer on 5 recordings), Norman Field (performer on 5 recordings), and Earle Ross (performer on 4 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to CBS Radio Network (broadcast on network) and Armed Forces Radio Service (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include illness, patients and recovery, Schenley Laboratories sponsorship, medicine and medical practice, medical ethics, duty and sacrifice, medical-themed literary and film adaptation, and medical biography and history.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Postwar American medical and scientific interest, CBS 1946 summer replacement season, Schenley Laboratories sponsorship, and Complete surviving thirteen-program run.
